questions.q: Glyceryl trioleate is boiled with aqueous NaOH. The products are:
options: Glycerol and oleic acid only, in equilibrium with the ester
questions.explain: Saponification of the triglyceride gives three molecules of sodium oleate (soap) and glycerol; in base the acid is trapped as its carboxylate, so the reaction goes to completion.

questions.q: Ethyl propanoate with ¹⁸O in its alkoxy (–O–C₂H₅) oxygen is saponified with NaOH. The ¹⁸O is found in:
questions.explain: BAC2 breaks the acyl–oxygen bond, so the alkoxy oxygen leaves with the ethyl group as ethanol. An SN2 attack on the ethyl carbon would have left the label in the propanoate.

questions.q: tert-Butyl acetate is hydrolysed in dilute acid containing H₂¹⁸O. Where does most of the ¹⁸O end up, and why?
options: In acetic acid, by AAC2 acyl–oxygen cleavage
In tert-butyl alcohol, by AAL1 alkyl–oxygen cleavage via a carbocation
In acetic acid, by AAL1 alkyl–oxygen cleavage
In tert-butyl alcohol, by BAC2 attack of water on the carbonyl
questions.explain: The protonated ester ionises at the O–C(CH₃)₃ bond to give a stable tertiary cation, which captures H₂¹⁸O, so the label appears in the alcohol. For normal esters (AAC2) the water oxygen ends up in the acid.

questions.q: A methyl ester is cleaved by a halide salt in DMSO, the nucleophile attacking the methyl carbon and the carboxylate leaving. In Ingold's notation this mechanism is:
questions.explain: It is base (nucleophile) promoted, breaks the alkyl–oxygen bond and has a bimolecular SN2-like slow step: BAL2.
